subproblem.title: Monotonicity, existence and upper semicontinuity of densities, and Θ ≥ 1 on the support, for minimizing cycles in a C² submanifold (Simon Ch. 4, §3 via 7.1.2; registered obligation)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n, d ∈ ℕ with 1 ≤ n ≤ d ≤ P, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, let N ⊆ ℝ^P be an embedded C² d-dimensional submanifold (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 d N) with (closure N ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, and let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) be minimizing in U ∩ N (IsMinimizingIn T (U ∩ N)) with spt T ⊆ U ∩ N and ∂T = 0 in U (BoundaryVanishes T). Then: (i) for every compact K ⊆ U there is Λ ≥ 0 such that for every y ∈ ℝ^P and R > 0 with closedBall y R ⊆ K the function ρ ↦ e^{Λρ}ρ^{−n}·M_{B_ρ(y)}(T) (in [0, ∞], written ofReal(e^{Λρ}/ρ^n)·T.massOn (ball y ρ)) is nondecreasing on (0, R); (ii) if N = ℝ^P, then for every y and R with B_R(y) ⊆ U the function ρ ↦ ρ^{−n}·M_{B_ρ(y)}(T) is nondecreasing on (0, R); (iii) there is Θ : ℝ^P → ℝ with HasMassDensity T y (Θ(y)) (Θ^n(μ_T, y) = Θ(y)) for every y ∈ U and Θ upper semicontinuous on U; (iv) if y ∈ spt T and HasMassDensity T y θ, then θ ≥ 1.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n d : ℕ) (U N : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n), 1 ≤ n → n ≤ d → d ≤ P → IsOpen U → IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 d N → (closure N \ N) ∩ U = ∅ → IsMinimizingIn T (U ∩ N) → T.support ⊆ U ∩ N → BoundaryVanishes T → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ Λ : ℝ, 0 ≤ Λ ∧ ∀ (y : Euclid P) (R : ℝ), closedBall y R ⊆ K → MonotoneOn (fun ρ : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (Λ * ρ) / ρ ^ n) * T.massOn (ball y ρ)) (Ioo 0 R)) ∧ (N = univ → ∀ (y : Euclid P) (R : ℝ), ball y R ⊆ U → MonotoneOn (fun ρ : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal (1 / ρ ^ n) * T.massOn (ball y ρ)) (Ioo 0 R)) ∧ (∃ Θ : Euclid P → ℝ, (∀ y ∈ U, HasMassDensity T y (Θ y)) ∧ UpperSemicontinuousOn Θ U) ∧ ∀ y ∈ T.support, ∀ θ : ℝ, HasMassDensity T y θ → 1 ≤ θ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Registration note (context, not part of the numbered proof). This child is a new obligation with a fresh Lean name. Its frozen type is byte-identical to that of DAG node root.dimension_reduction_results-a1.monotonicity-a1 (Submission.dimred_minimizing_monotonicity, status rlcr-lean), which is not comparator-accepted and is owned by another parent; the runtime forbids reusing it here, and ancestor dependencies are not inherited by the selected node. The numbered proof below is that node's parent-supplied natural proof, which was accepted in the decomposition audit of root.dimension_reduction_results-a1. It is reproduced unchanged except that its prerequisite references are re-targeted to registered siblings of this split: minimizing_implies_stationary → sibling child stationarity (Submission.idtp_fons_minimizing_stationary, same frozen type MinimizingImpliesStationary); im_mass_measure → sibling child im_mass_measure (the same accepted declaration). Its 'Source: parent step …' line refers to the proof of root.dimension_reduction_results-a1. The numbered proof below is complete as it stands; exact-type reuse of the identically typed node, once that node is comparator-accepted, would be an alternative way to discharge the same type.

Source: parent step T1, i.e. Simon Ch. 4, 3.1–3.17 and 3.11 (chapter-04.txt lines 215–430) applied to the varifold of T through the sibling child stationarity; the computations are written out. Write ω_n := unitBallVolume n ∈ (0, ∞).
0. (Setting.) Put k := P − n and ℓ := d − n; then P = n + k, d = n + ℓ and ℓ ≤ k. Transporting along the equality Euclid P = Euclid (n + k) (nothing else changes), the hypotheses are exactly those of the sibling child stationarity (Submission.idtp_fons_minimizing_stationary, frozen type MinimizingImpliesStationary). T is integer multiplicity (first conjunct of IsMinimizingIn); fix a representation R = (M, θ, ξ) and put μ := R.measure = θ·H^n⌞M and V := v(M, θ). By the sibling child stationarity, R.HasLocallyBoundedMeanCurvature: there is a μ-measurable H : ℝ^P → ℝ^P such that δV(X) := ∫ div_M X dμ = −∫ X·H dμ for every C¹ vector field X with compact support in U (div_M X(x) = trace(p_{T_xM} ∘ DX(x)), T_xM the approximate tangent plane, which exists μ-a.e.), and for every compact K ⊆ U there is Λ_K with |H| ≤ Λ_K μ-a.e. on K; and R.IsStationaryAlong N. By the sibling child im_mass_measure (a), M_W(T) = μ(W) for every open W ⊆ U; these values are finite when closure W is a compact subset of U.
1. (Differential identity; Simon 3.2–3.4 and 3.16.) Fix a compact K ⊆ U, Λ := max(Λ_K, 0), y ∈ ℝ^P and R > 0 with closedBall y R ⊆ K, ε ∈ (0, 1), and φ ∈ C¹(ℝ; [0, 1]) with φ' ≤ 0, φ = 1 on (−∞, 1] and φ = 0 on [1 + ε, ∞). For ρ ∈ (0, R/(1 + ε)) let X_ρ(x) := φ(|x − y|/ρ)(x − y), a C¹ vector field with support in closedBall y ((1 + ε)ρ) ⊆ K. With r := |x − y| and D^⊥r the component of (x − y)/r orthogonal to T_xM, at μ-a.e. x we have div_M X_ρ = n·φ(r/ρ) + (r/ρ)φ'(r/ρ)(1 − |D^⊥r|²) (Simon 3.2: ∇^M φ(r/ρ) = ρ^{−1}φ'(r/ρ) p_{T_xM}((x − y)/r) and div_M(x − y) = n). Put I(ρ) := ∫ φ(r/ρ) dμ and J(ρ) := ∫ φ(r/ρ)|D^⊥r|² dμ; both are differentiable in ρ with derivatives obtained by differentiating under the integral sign (φ' is bounded and all integrands vanish outside K). Since (r/ρ)φ'(r/ρ) = −ρ·∂_ρ[φ(r/ρ)], the identity δV(X_ρ) = −∫ X_ρ·H dμ reads n·I(ρ) − ρI'(ρ) = −ρJ'(ρ) − ∫ φ(r/ρ)(x − y)·H dμ, i.e. d/dρ(ρ^{−n}I(ρ)) = ρ^{−n}J'(ρ) + ρ^{−n−1}∫ φ(r/ρ)(x − y)·H dμ.
2. (Monotonicity on closed balls; Simon 3.17.) J is nondecreasing in ρ (φ(r/ρ) is nondecreasing in ρ because φ' ≤ 0), so J' ≥ 0. On the support of φ(r/ρ) we have |x − y| ≤ (1 + ε)ρ and |H| ≤ Λ μ-a.e., so the last term is ≥ −(1 + ε)Λρ^{−n}I(ρ). Hence d/dρ(e^{(1+ε)Λρ}ρ^{−n}I(ρ)) ≥ 0, and e^{(1+ε)Λρ}ρ^{−n}I(ρ) is nondecreasing on (0, R/(1 + ε)). Let ε ↓ 0 along a sequence of such φ = φ_ε decreasing pointwise to the indicator of (−∞, 1]; by dominated convergence I_ε(ρ) → μ(closedBall y ρ). Hence e^{Λσ}σ^{−n}μ(closedBall y σ) ≤ e^{Λρ}ρ^{−n}μ(closedBall y ρ) for 0 < σ < ρ < R. (This is the statement of SimonGMT HasGeneralizedMeanCurvatureIn.exp_normalizedBallMass_monotoneOn for the library's varifold structure.)
3. ((i).) Let 0 < σ < ρ < R and σ ≤ s < ρ. Then e^{Λσ}σ^{−n}μ(B_σ(y)) ≤ e^{Λσ}σ^{−n}μ(closedBall y σ) ≤ e^{Λs}s^{−n}μ(closedBall y s) ≤ e^{Λs}s^{−n}μ(B_ρ(y)), and letting s ↑ ρ gives e^{Λσ}σ^{−n}μ(B_σ(y)) ≤ e^{Λρ}ρ^{−n}μ(B_ρ(y)). As B_ρ(y) ⊆ K ⊆ U is open, μ(B_ρ(y)) = M_{B_ρ(y)}(T) (step 0), so ρ ↦ ofReal(e^{Λρ}/ρ^n)·M_{B_ρ(y)}(T) is nondecreasing on (0, R). Λ depends only on K, as required.
4. ((ii).) If N = ℝ^P, every vector v is tangent to N at every point (take γ(t) := x + tv in the definition of tangentSpace), so R.IsStationaryAlong N says δV(X) = 0 for every C¹ field X with compact support in U. Then steps 1–3 hold with the H-term replaced by 0, i.e. with Λ = 0, on every closed ball closedBall y R' ⊆ U. If B_R(y) ⊆ U and 0 < σ < ρ < R, choose R' ∈ (ρ, R); closedBall y R' ⊆ B_R(y) ⊆ U, and the Λ = 0 version of step 3 on (0, R') compares σ and ρ.
5. ((iii).) Let y ∈ U; choose R > 0 with K := closedBall y R ⊆ U and Λ as in (i). g(ρ) := e^{Λρ}ρ^{−n}μ(B_ρ(y)) is nondecreasing, nonnegative and finite on (0, R), so g(ρ) → L := inf g ∈ [0, ∞) as ρ ↓ 0, and ρ^{−n}μ(B_ρ(y)) = e^{−Λρ}g(ρ) → L. With θ := L/ω_n ≥ 0 we get M_{B_ρ(y)}(T)/(ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n)) → ofReal θ as ρ ↓ 0, i.e. HasMassDensity T y θ. Limits in [0, ∞] are unique, so this θ is unique; call it Θ(y), and put Θ(y) := 0 for y ∉ U.
6. ((iii), upper semicontinuity; Simon 3.11.) Θ of step 5 satisfies HasMassDensity T y (Θ(y)) for y ∈ U. To see that Θ is upper semicontinuous on U, let y_j → y with y_j, y ∈ U, choose R > 0 with closedBall y (2R) ⊆ U and Λ for K := closedBall y (2R), and let ρ, η > 0 with ρ + η < R. For large j, |y_j − y| < η, so closedBall y_j R ⊆ K and, by step 5 and monotonicity at y_j, Θ(y_j) ≤ e^{Λρ}μ(B_ρ(y_j))/(ω_nρ^n) ≤ e^{Λρ}μ(B_{ρ+η}(y))/(ω_nρ^n). Hence limsup_j Θ(y_j) ≤ e^{Λρ}μ(closedBall y (ρ + η))/(ω_nρ^n); letting η ↓ 0 replaces closedBall y (ρ + η) by closedBall y ρ, and letting ρ ↓ 0 gives limsup_j Θ(y_j) ≤ Θ(y), because (ω_nρ^n)^{−1}μ(closedBall y ρ) → Θ(y) as well (for s < ρ < s', μ(B_ρ(y)) ≤ μ(closedBall y ρ) ≤ μ(B_{s'}(y))).
7. ((iv).) For H^n-a.e. x ∈ M, Θ^n(μ, x) = θ(x) (Simon Ch. 3, Theorem 1.9 together with Ch. 4, Remark 1.8(2), as used at chapter-04.txt line 350: H^n⌞M has density 1 at H^n-a.e. point of the countably n-rectifiable set M, and H^n⌞M-a.e. point of M is a Lebesgue point of the locally integrable θ); since θ ≥ 1 on M, Θ ≥ 1 μ-a.e. Let y ∈ spt T and HasMassDensity T y θ_y; by uniqueness θ_y = Θ(y). By im_mass_measure (b), μ(B_ε(y)) > 0 for every ε > 0, so every small ball B_ε(y) ⊆ U contains a point z_ε with Θ(z_ε) ≥ 1. By step 6, θ_y = Θ(y) ≥ limsup_{ε↓0} Θ(z_ε) ≥ 1.
proof_key_steps: The sibling child stationarity gives a representation whose varifold has generalized mean curvature bounded on compacts (and zero when N = ℝ^P); im_mass_measure identifies masses with the varifold weight.
First-variation identity with radial fields X = φ(r/ρ)(x − y) gives d/dρ(ρ^{−n}I) ≥ −Λρ^{−n}I, hence e^{Λρ}ρ^{−n}μ(B̄_ρ) is nondecreasing; pass to open balls.
Monotone limits give existence of Θ^n at every point of U; the 3.11 argument gives upper semicontinuity of Θ on U.
Θ = θ ≥ 1 μ-a.e. plus upper semicontinuity give Θ ≥ 1 on spt T.

audit.reason: The registered stationarity and mass-measure prerequisites support the radial first-variation computation. The proof correctly passes from closed to open balls, constructs finite nonnegative density limits, proves upper semicontinuity, and extends the almost-everywhere integer lower bound to every support point.
